keyVerseText: Of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
rootMeaning: The root of פִּלְטַי (Pilṭay) is connected to פַּלְטִי (Palṭîy), which means 'escape' or 'deliverance.' This root sense conveys the idea of rescue or being set free, which goes beyond a mere personal name to embody a concept of divine or providential deliverance. Thus, Pilṭay can be understood as 'my deliverances,' emphasizing a personal testimony of rescue that may reflect God's saving work.
usageInScripture: Pilṭay appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Nehemiah 12:17, where it is used as a proper name of a priest associated with the priestly house of Moadiah. The singular occurrence and consistent translation as 'Piltai' indicate that the word functions primarily as a proper noun rather than a common noun, highlighting an individual who was part of the post-exilic community returning under Zerubbabel's leadership.
theologicalSignificance: The name Pilṭay, meaning 'my deliverances,' carries rich theological significance as it points to God's faithfulness in rescuing His people. As a priest and representative of a priestly lineage, Pilṭay symbolizes the continuity of worship and the preservation of covenant identity after exile. This reminds believers that God not only delivers but also restores and reestablishes His people to serve Him. In Christ, the ultimate Deliverer, this name anticipates the spiritual rescue and priestly mediation that Jesus fulfills on behalf of His people.
keyVerseReflection: Nehemiah 12:17 lists Pilṭay among the priests of the house of Moadiah who returned from exile, emphasizing their role in reestablishing temple worship. The inclusion of Pilṭay's name, meaning 'my deliverances,' in this verse underscores the theme of God's saving hand in the restoration era. It highlights that the community’s return and renewed worship are not merely historical events but testimonies to God's ongoing deliverance and faithfulness.
